limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema cannot show whether an item actually requires tense selection rather than merely presents a tense form.
name: Finite tense contrast
pedagogical_interpretation: Learners may improve in selecting and interpreting present versus past finite-tense forms in non-modal clauses.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema does not distinguish do-support, auxiliary negation, contracted forms, or the scope and meaning of negation.
name: Clause negation
pedagogical_interpretation: Learners may improve in forming and interpreting negative clauses across available constructions.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema cannot establish whether progressive meaning, auxiliary morphology, or lexical aspect is the source of difficulty.
name: Progressive auxiliary chain
pedagogical_interpretation: Learners may improve in using progressive aspect within finite and modal constructions.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The cell representation does not distinguish experiential, resultative, continuative, or anteriority uses of the perfect.
name: Perfect auxiliary chain
pedagogical_interpretation: Learners may improve in using perfect aspect, including its auxiliary sequence, across finite and modal clauses.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: Evidence from item errors is needed to determine whether this combined construction warrants a distinct KC beyond the two component hypotheses.

pedagogical_interpretation: Learners may improve in coordinating perfect and progressive auxiliaries in the combined aspect construction.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema does not encode participle morphology, agent phrases, verb transitivity, or whether passive voice is required by the task.
name: Passive voice construction
pedagogical_interpretation: Learners may improve in producing or recognizing canonical BE-passive clauses across tense, aspect, polarity, and modal contexts.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema cannot distinguish auxiliary inversion from intonation questions, nor show whether question formation is elicited rather than supplied.
name: Polar question formation
pedagogical_interpretation: Learners may improve in forming or interpreting yes-no questions, including auxiliary-fronting patterns where relevant.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: No supported subject-wh-question cell is present, and the schema omits wh-word identity, gap position, and inversion details.
name: Wh-question formation
pedagogical_interpretation: Learners may improve in forming or interpreting information questions with a questioned non-subject constituent.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema cannot distinguish directive force, politeness, lexical verb choice, or imperative forms involving do-support.
name: Imperative construction
pedagogical_interpretation: Learners may improve in using positive and negative imperative clauses for instructions or commands.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema records modal identity but not modal function, register, conditional meaning, or whether the task requires form versus interpretation.
name: Modal auxiliary construction
pedagogical_interpretation: Learners may improve in placing and interpreting a central modal auxiliary with a non-finite verbal chain.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema cannot tell whether learners treat modal perfects as a common construction or as modal-specific meanings requiring separate knowledge.
name: Modal perfect construction
pedagogical_interpretation: Learners may improve in combining a modal with a perfect auxiliary chain.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: Only a limited set of modal identities is represented with progressive aspect, so broader generalization needs additional cells and items.
name: Modal progressive construction
pedagogical_interpretation: Learners may improve in combining a modal with progressive aspect.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The universe supports only will for this combination; items with other modals are needed to test whether the hypothesis is genuinely reusable.
name: Modal perfect-progressive construction
pedagogical_interpretation: Learners may improve in coordinating modal, perfect, and progressive auxiliaries in one verbal chain.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema lacks ability, permission, possibility, politeness, and counterfactual-use distinctions, which may require separate treatment.
name: Can and could modal contrast
pedagogical_interpretation: Learners may improve in using can/could forms in declarative, negative, perfect, and question constructions.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema cannot identify epistemic versus permission uses, so the family label requires item semantics and validation evidence.
name: Epistemic possibility modal set
pedagogical_interpretation: Learners may improve in using may and might forms in the available clause constructions.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: Must and should have distinct force and negative interpretations; item-level meaning and learner-response evidence are required before combining them in an ontology.
name: Obligation and advice modal set
pedagogical_interpretation: Learners may improve in using must and should forms, including their negative and perfect configurations.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema cannot distinguish futurity, willingness, prediction, conditionality, or politeness, so the proposed grouping is provisional.
name: Will and would modal set
pedagogical_interpretation: Learners may improve in using will/would forms across declarative, perfect, progressive, and polar-question contexts.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema supplies no temporal learning data, morphology, or dependency evidence, so prerequisite status cannot be inferred from these cells alone.
name: Passive auxiliary-chain prerequisite
pedagogical_interpretation: Learners may need a stable ability to coordinate BE with passive-participle structure before reliably handling passive clauses with tense or aspect.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema cannot show subject agreement, lexical verb morphology, or whether items actually require production rather than recognition.
name: Present simple declaratives
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve forming and interpreting present-tense simple affirmative statements.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: Regular versus irregular morphology and temporal discourse use are not represented in the GrammarCell.
name: Past simple declaratives
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve forming and interpreting past-tense simple affirmative statements.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema does not distinguish do-support from other negative auxiliary patterns or contracted from uncontracted forms.
name: Finite declarative negation
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve constructing or interpreting negative finite active declarative clauses.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema cannot establish whether progressive meaning, participle morphology, and auxiliary selection should be learned together.
name: Progressive aspect
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve use of the progressive auxiliary-and-participle sequence to present an event as ongoing.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema does not distinguish experiential, resultative, continuative, or anterior modal uses of the perfect.
name: Perfect aspect
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve use of the perfect auxiliary-and-participle sequence.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema cannot determine whether this combination is best modeled as an independent KC or as successful composition of separate perfect and progressive knowledge.
name: Perfect progressive aspect
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve assembling and interpreting the combined perfect-progressive auxiliary chain.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema omits agent phrases, participle morphology, adjectival-passive ambiguity, and whether a passive transformation is demanded.
name: Canonical passive voice
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve identifying or forming clauses in which the patient is realized as the clause subject with a BE-passive.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema does not expose word order, intonation, answer expectations, or whether an item requires auxiliary inversion.
name: Polar question formation
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve recognizing or producing yes/no question clause structure.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: No subject-WH cells are present, and the schema lacks WH-word identity, extraction role, and inversion details.

pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve interpreting or forming information questions with a non-subject WH element.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema does not distinguish prohibitives, politeness, addressee reference, or pragmatic force.

pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve interpreting and forming direct affirmative and negative commands.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: Modal identity does not reveal intended meaning, and the schema cannot show whether different modals require separate lexical-semantic knowledge.
name: Modal auxiliary constructions
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve handling the basic modal-plus-verb construction across modal identities.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema cannot distinguish scope, contraction, modal-specific semantic effects, or whether negation attaches to a modal in the learner-facing wording.
name: Modal negation
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve using and interpreting negation in modal clauses.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema cannot determine whether learners treat modal-perfect forms as an independent pattern or compose independently mastered modal and perfect operations.
name: Modal perfect chain
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve constructing or interpreting a modal followed by a perfect auxiliary chain.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: Only a restricted set of modal-progressive combinations occurs in this universe, so broader reuse needs additional grammar or item evidence.
name: Modal progressive chain
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve constructing or interpreting a modal followed by a progressive auxiliary chain.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: This universe supplies only WILL realizations, so it cannot establish whether the pattern generalizes across modals or is independently measurable.
name: Modal perfect-progressive chain
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve managing the extended modal-perfect-progressive auxiliary sequence.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema does not show participle accuracy or establish whether perfect and passive are independently recoverable from items.
name: Perfect passive construction
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve forming or interpreting the combined perfect and passive auxiliary sequence.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The universe is limited to present and past declaratives, so transfer to questions, modals, or other contexts cannot be assessed.
name: Progressive passive construction
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve forming or interpreting progressive clauses in the passive voice.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema cannot distinguish auxiliary negation placement, contraction, and negative scope; an item bank is needed to test separability from general negation and passive voice.
name: Passive polarity handling
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve maintaining clause polarity while constructing or interpreting passive clauses.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema does not identify lexical verb morphology, agreement, copular versus lexical predicates, or whether the task actually elicits the finite form.
name: present-tense finite clause
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve production or recognition of present-tense finite forms in non-modal clauses.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema cannot distinguish regular from irregular morphology, auxiliary selection, or lexical-semantic uses of past forms.
name: past-tense finite clause
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve production or recognition of past-tense finite forms in non-modal clauses.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema does not show progressive participle morphology, stative-verb restrictions, or whether progressive meaning is intended in context.
name: progressive auxiliary chain
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve use of the progressive auxiliary-and-participle sequence across tense, polarity, voice, and modal environments.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema lacks participle identity and contextual interpretation, so it cannot separate experiential, resultative, continuative, or other perfect uses.
name: perfect auxiliary chain
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve use of the perfect auxiliary-and-past-participle sequence across available constructions.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema does not reveal the actual auxiliary sequence, participle realization, duration meanings, or whether learners treat this as a compositional combination.
name: perfect-progressive auxiliary chain
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve management of the combined perfect and progressive auxiliary sequence.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema cannot identify agent phrases, adjectival-passive ambiguity, lexical restrictions, or whether the task targets voice rather than an associated form.
name: passive voice construction
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve formation or interpretation of canonical BE-passives across available tense and aspect forms.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema does not distinguish not from contracted forms, do-support, negative imperatives, scope, or lexical negative expressions.
name: clausal negation
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve placement and realization of clause-level negation in available auxiliary environments.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema does not encode word order, intonation, subject type, auxiliary inversion, or whether the prompt requires question formation.
name: polar-question formation
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve formation or interpretation of yes/no questions in the represented auxiliary configurations.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema does not identify the wh-word, extraction site, inversion pattern, or whether subject and non-subject questions are empirically separable for learners.
name: wh-question formation
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve recognition or formation of wh-questions across subject and non-subject question types.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema does not encode imperative subject realization, do-support in negative imperatives, pragmatic force, or politeness.
name: imperative construction
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve use or interpretation of positive and negative imperative clauses.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema identifies modal words but not their meanings, register, polarity effects, or lexicalized uses; it therefore cannot justify a modal-function ontology.

pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve use of a central modal as the finite verbal element in a clause.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema cannot establish whether modal-perfect combinations share a learner representation or whether individual modal meanings require different instruction.

pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve combining a central modal with a perfect auxiliary sequence.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema does not expose auxiliary order or determine whether progressive and perfect-progressive modal sequences should be learned together.

pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve combining a central modal with a progressive auxiliary sequence.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema cannot distinguish contracted forms, semantic scope, prohibition versus inference readings, or idiosyncratic forms such as cannot.
name: modal negation
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve the placement and realization of negation with a central modal.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema does not provide inversion details, discourse function, or evidence that modal-question form is distinct from general polar-question and modal knowledge.
name: modal polar question
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve use of a central modal in yes/no question form.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema cannot distinguish present-perfect meanings, adverbial cues, lexical aspect, or whether passive and active present perfect should share one KC.
name: present perfect finite construction
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve use of present-tense perfect constructions, including their active and passive realizations.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema lacks event ordering, discourse context, lexical aspect, and evidence that learners distinguish past perfect from the general perfect operation.
name: past perfect finite construction
pedagogical_interpretation: Practice may improve use of past-tense perfect constructions, including active and passive realizations.

limitation_or_needed_evidence: The schema does not reveal the realized auxiliary chain, agent structure, lexical verb constraints, or whether this combination is best modeled compositionally.
